course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

topic.title: Exponential Functions
topic.summary: The general form f(x) = abˣ, its initial value and base, exponential growth and decay, why exponential functions have no extrema or points of inflection, and their end behavior.

variants.stem: The exponential function f is given by f(x) = 6(1/3)ˣ.

parts.prompt: Find the initial value of f.
Find the base of f.
Does f demonstrate exponential growth or exponential decay?

solution: In the general form f(x) = abˣ, the initial value is a = f(0) = 6.
The base is b = 1/3.
Because a > 0 and 0 < b < 1, f demonstrates exponential decay.

parts.prompt: Find the limit as x increases without bound.
Find the limit as x decreases without bound.

solution: Since 0 < b < 1, bˣ gets arbitrarily close to 0 as x → ∞ and grows without bound as x → −∞.
Multiplying by a = 2, which is positive, keeps the sign of the outputs. So lim x→∞ f(x) = 0 and lim x→−∞ f(x) = ∞.

parts.prompt: Write the domain of f in interval notation.
Write the range of f in interval notation.
Write the equation of the horizontal asymptote.

solution: An exponential function is defined for every real number x, so the domain is (−∞, ∞).
The factor 4ˣ is always positive, so the outputs have the same sign as a = 2. The range is (0, ∞).
The outputs get arbitrarily close to 0 but never reach it, so the horizontal asymptote is y = 0.
